questions.question_english: What is the legal effect and significance of Section 42A, inserted into the POCSO Act, 2012?
options_english: It mandates that the POSH Act, 2013 shall override the POCSO Act in all educational institutions.
It provides that the POCSO Act shall have an overriding effect over any inconsistent provisions in other laws.
It confers complete procedural immunity upon school principals and teachers against false criminal allegations.
It transfers the judicial jurisdiction of all child abuse cases exclusively to local Family Courts.
questions.explanation_english:
Section 42A of the POCSO Act contains a non-obstante clause that establishes the statutory supremacy of the POCSO Act. It states:
'The provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law for the time being in force or in any instrument having effect by virtue of any law other than this Act.'
This overriding clause ensures that whenever there is any operational conflict or inconsistency between the child-protection provisions of the POCSO Act and any general or procedural provisions of other statutes (such as the CrPC/BNSS, IPC/BNS, POSH Act, or state education acts), the provisions of the POCSO Act will prevail to ensure the paramount interest and protection of children.
questions.explanation_hindi:
पॉक्सो अधिनियम की धारा 42A में एक 'अध्यारोही खंड' (non-obstante clause) शामिल है, जो स्पष्ट करता है कि:
'इस अधिनियम के उपबंध, तत्समय प्रवृत्त किसी अन्य विधि में अथवा इस अधिनियम से भिन्न किसी विधि के आधार पर प्रभावी किसी दस्तावेज में अंतर्विष्ट किसी असंगत बात के होते हुए भी प्रभावी होंगे।' (Act not in derogation of any other law; overriding effect).
इसका अर्थ है कि यदि बाल संरक्षण के मामलों में पॉक्सो अधिनियम और किसी अन्य सामान्य या विशेष कानून (जैसे POSH, CrPC, या राज्य शिक्षा संहिता) के बीच कोई विधिक असंगति या टकराव होता है, तो पॉक्सो अधिनियम के प्रावधान ही सर्वोपरि मान्य होंगे। अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english: A Head Clerk in a school manipulates accounts and embezzles Rs. 5 Lakhs. A departmental inquiry proves the charge beyond doubt. questions.question_english: Under the Income Tax Act, 1961, what does the acronym "TAN" stand for?
options_english: Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number
Tax Assessment and Registration Number
Taxpayer Identification and Allocation Number
Tax Allotment Number
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 203A of the Income Tax Act, 1961, TAN stands for 'Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number'. It is a unique 10-digit alphanumeric identifier issued by the Income Tax Department to all persons and offices responsible for deducting tax at source (TDS) or collecting tax at source (TCS). Every Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) in a school or government office must obtain a TAN and quote it mandatorily in all TDS challans, quarterly TDS statements (e.g., Form 24Q for salaries), and Form 16 certificates issued to employees.
questions.explanation_hindi: आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 203A के तहत, TAN का पूर्ण रूप 'Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number' (कर कटौती और संग्रह खाता संख्या) है। यह 10 वर्णों (अक्षरों और अंकों) का एक विशिष्ट पहचान कोड है जो आयकर विभाग द्वारा उन सभी व्यक्तियों और कार्यालयों को जारी किया जाता है जो स्रोत पर कर कटौती (TDS) या संग्रह (TCS) के लिए उत्तरदायी हैं। प्रत्येक स्कूल या सरकारी कार्यालय के आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) के लिए TAN प्राप्त करना और इसे सभी टीडीएस चालान, त्रैमासिक रिटर्न (जैसे वेतन के लिए Form 24Q) और फॉर्म 16 प्रमाणपत्रों में लिखना अनिवार्य है।

questions.question_english: To facilitate fair examination participation for children with disabilities, Central and State examination boards provide designated accommodations. Which of the following is NOT a permissible or mandated accommodation?
options_english: Provision of an amanuensis (scribe) or reader
Complete exemption from all continuous and comprehensive evaluations (CCE) and assessments
Compensatory extra time to complete the examination
Alternative objective or adapted questions in lieu of descriptive or visual/diagram-based questions
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 16(vi) of the RPwD Act, 2016 and examination guidelines issued by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MSJE), CBSE, and State Boards, reasonable accommodations during examinations include:
1. Provision of an amanuensis (scribe), reader, or lab assistant.
2. Compensatory time of not less than 20 minutes per hour of examination.
3. Adapted/alternative questions in lieu of visual diagrams or map-work for visually impaired candidates.
4. Facility to use assistive technology, computers, Braille sheets, or large-print question papers.
5. Exemption from second/third language requirements.

However, 'complete exemption from all continuous and comprehensive evaluations (CCE)' is NOT a permissible accommodation. Evaluation and assessment are indispensable components of the educational process to identify learning gaps and design individualized education plans (IEPs). Rather than exempting a child entirely from assessment, the modes, tools, and formatting of evaluation must be suitably adapted.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 16(vi) तथा केंद्रीय सामाजिक न्याय एवं अधिकारिता मंत्रालय और विभिन्न परीक्षा बोर्डों (जैसे CBSE) द्वारा जारी दिशा-निर्देशों के अनुसार परीक्षा में दी जाने वाली सुविधाओं में निम्नलिखित शामिल हैं:
1. श्रुतलेखक (स्क्राइब), वाचक अथवा प्रयोगशाला सहायक की सुविधा।
2. प्रति घंटे कम से कम 20 मिनट का प्रतिपूरक (अतिरिक्त) समय।
3. दृष्टिबाधित परीक्षार्थियों के लिए रेखाचित्रों/मानचित्रों के स्थान पर वैकल्पिक वस्तुनिष्ठ प्रश्न।
4. ब्रेल लिपि, बड़े अक्षरों वाले प्रश्नपत्र या कंप्यूटर का उपयोग करने की अनुमति।
5. द्वितीय/तृतीय भाषा के अध्ययन से छूट।

किंतु 'समस्त सतत एवं व्यापक मूल्यांकन (CCE) और आकलनों से पूर्ण छूट' कोई मान्य सुविधा नहीं है। मूल्यांकन विद्यार्थी के शैक्षणिक विकास व अधिगम स्तर को जानने का अनिवार्य अंग है। समावेशी शिक्षा का उद्देश्य मूल्यांकन को पूरी तरह समाप्त करना नहीं, बल्कि मूल्यांकन की पद्धतियों को बच्चे की दिव्यांगता के अनुरूप अनुकूलित (adapt) करना है।

questions.explanation_english:
The fundamental distinction between Article 15(4) and Article 16(4) of the Constitution of India lies in their distinct functional domains:

1. Article 15(4): Inserted by the First Constitutional Amendment Act of 1951 (following the landmark State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan case), Article 15(4) is a general enabling provision. It empowers the State to make 'special provisions for the advancement of any socially and educationally backward classes of citizens or for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes.' In educational governance and administrative practice, this provides the constitutional authority for affirmative action in education, including fee concessions, age relaxations, and reserved quotas in admission to state-run or state-aided colleges and universities.

2. Its scope is confined strictly to public services, recruitment rosters, and employment under the Union or State Governments, including appointments in government school systems.

questions.question_english: Upon completing an inquiry under the POSH Act, 2013 and arriving at a finding that the allegations of sexual harassment are proved, can the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) recommend financial compensation/penalty against the respondent?

questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 13(3) of the POSH Act, 2013, where the Internal Committee arrives at the conclusion that the allegation against the respondent has been proved, it shall recommend to the employer:
1. To take disciplinary action for sexual harassment as a misconduct in accordance with the applicable service rules;
2. To deduct from the salary or wages of the respondent such sum as it may consider appropriate to be paid to the aggrieved woman or to her legal heirs, in accordance with the determination of compensation under Section 15 of the Act.
If the employer is unable to deduct such compensation due to respondent's absence from duty or cessation of employment, the committee may direct the respondent to pay such sum directly, and upon default, it can be recovered as an arrear of land revenue (Section 13(3)(ii)). There is no arbitrary Rs. 10,000 cap; Section 15 outlines factors like mental trauma, medical expenses, lost career opportunities, and the financial status of the respondent.

questions.question_english: What does the term "Own Merit Candidate" (also known as Meritorious Reserved Candidate - MRC) mean in the context of government recruitment and post-based reservation rosters?
options_english: A reserved candidate selected on open merit without relaxed standards
A reserved candidate who receives a government merit scholarship for study
A candidate who successfully clears the competitive exam in their first attempt
A candidate applying exclusively for unreserved posts who forfeits caste benefits
questions.explanation_english: In constitutional law and service jurisprudence (reiterated in the landmark Indra Sawhney judgment and DoPT OM No. 36012/23/96-Estt.(Res)), an 'Own Merit Candidate' or 'Meritorious Reserved Candidate' (MRC) is a candidate belonging to a reserved category (SC, ST, OBC, or EWS) who secures selection purely on the basis of open general merit without availing any concession or relaxed standard at any stage of the recruitment process (such as relaxation in age limit, experience, educational cut-off marks, or examination fees). Such candidates are appointed against the unreserved (UR) points of the reservation roster and are not counted against the quota reserved for their respective categories. This ensures that the reserved quota remains entirely available for other reserved category candidates.

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): If an employee opts for the New Tax Regime, they can still claim the deduction for interest on a home loan under Section 24(b) for a let-out (rented) property.
Reason (R): The restriction under Section 115BAC for Section 24(b) applies only to self-occupied properties.
In the context of the above statements, which of the following is correct?
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and Reason (R) is the accurate statutory explanation for Assertion (A). Under the New Tax Regime governed by Section 115BAC of the Income Tax Act, 1961, deductions for housing loan interest under Section 24(b) are expressly disallowed for 'self-occupied' house properties (where loss cannot be set off against salaries). However, for 'let-out' or rented properties, Section 24(b) interest deduction is fully allowable against the rental income to compute net income from house property. It is important to note that while interest is deductible against rent, any net loss under the head House Property cannot be set off against Salary income under Section 115BAC.

questions.question_english: In the landmark case of Pramati Educational & Cultural Trust v. Union of India, the Supreme Court validated Article 15(5). What was the core ruling regarding its applicability to the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009?
options_english: The RTE Act 25% quota applies equally to minority and non-minority private unaided schools
RTE Act 25% quota does not apply to minority educational institutions
The RTE Act in its entirety is ultra vires of Article 19(1)(g) fundamental freedom
All private unaided schools are completely exempt from providing 25% seat reservation
questions.explanation_english: In Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust v. Union of India (2014) 8 SCC 1, a five-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court examined the validity of Article 15(5) (inserted by the 93rd Amendment) and Article 21A (inserted by the 86th Amendment). The Court upheld the constitutional validity of both amendments and validated the 25% reservation quota under Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act, 2009 for private unaided non-minority schools. However, the Court definitively held that the RTE Act, 2009, insofar as it applies to minority educational institutions (whether aided or unaided), violates the fundamental rights guaranteed to religious and linguistic minorities under Article 30(1). Consequently, the Court held that the RTE Act's 25% admission quota does not apply to minority schools.

questions.question_english: Under Section 80D of the Income Tax Act, 1961, what is the maximum deduction allowed for medical insurance premiums paid by an individual employee for self, spouse, and dependent children (assuming none is a senior citizen)?
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 80D of the Income Tax Act, 1961, the deductions available for health insurance premiums are structured as follows:
1. Self, spouse, and dependent children: An individual taxpayer is entitled to a deduction of up to ₹25,000 per financial year for health insurance premiums paid by any mode other than cash, provided no covered person is 60 years or older (senior citizen).
2. Preventive Health Check-up: Within this overall cap of ₹25,000, up to ₹5,000 is permitted for preventive health check-up expenses (which may be paid in cash).
3. Senior Citizens: If the insured individual or spouse is a senior citizen (60 years or above), the deduction limit increases to ₹50,000.
4. Parents: A separate, additional deduction of up to ₹25,000 (or ₹50,000 if parents are senior citizens) is available for health insurance on parents.
Since the question specifies self, spouse, and dependent children with none being a senior citizen, the maximum permissible deduction is ₹25,000.

1. एक व्यक्तिगत करदाता अपने, अपने जीवनसाथी और आश्रित बच्चों के लिए भुगतान किए गए स्वास्थ्य बीमा प्रीमियम पर प्रति वित्तीय वर्ष ₹25,000 तक की कटौती प्राप्त कर सकता है, बशर्ते उनमें से कोई भी वरिष्ठ नागरिक (60 वर्ष या उससे अधिक) न हो।

questions.question_english: A newly recruited Post Graduate Teacher (PGT) joins a government school in September. The teacher had previously worked in an aided/private school from April to August of the same financial year. For the purpose of deducting TDS under Section 192, what is the statutory duty of the current DDO?
options_english: Consider exclusively the salary paid by the government school and disregard the previous employment completely.
Formally instruct the employee to prepare and file two separate annual income tax returns for the two employments.
Obtain details of salary paid and TDS deducted by the previous employer in Form 12B and compute TDS on aggregate salary.
Refrain from deducting TDS as the DDO has no jurisdiction over mid-year appointments.
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 192(2) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 read with Rule 26A of the Income Tax Rules, where an assessee is employed simultaneously under more than one employer, or where he has held successive employments under more than one employer during the financial year, he may furnish to the current employer/DDO details of salary and TDS from the other/previous employer in Form 12B.

Upon receiving Form 12B verified by the employee, the current DDO must:
1. Aggregate the previous salary and current salary for the entire financial year.
2. Deduct allowable deductions across the full year.
3. Compute the overall annual tax liability.
4. Give credit for TDS already deducted by the previous employer, and deduct the balance tax in equal monthly installments over the remaining months (September to March).

If the previous salary is ignored, the employee would end up receiving standard deduction and basic exemption twice, leading to significant under-deduction of tax.
questions.explanation_hindi:
आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 192(2) और आयकर नियम के नियम 26A के अनुसार, जब कोई कर्मचारी वित्तीय वर्ष के दौरान एक से अधिक नियोक्ताओं के अधीन कार्य करता है या वर्ष के मध्य में नौकरी बदलता है, तो वह फॉर्म 12B में पिछले नियोक्ता से प्राप्त वेतन और काटे गए टीडीएस का विवरण वर्तमान नियोक्ता/DDO को प्रस्तुत कर सकता है।

कर्मचारी द्वारा सत्यापित फॉर्म 12B प्राप्त करने पर वर्तमान DDO का यह दायित्व है कि:
1. पूरे वित्तीय वर्ष के लिए पिछले और वर्तमान वेतन को संयोजित (Aggregate) करे।
2. पूरे वर्ष के लिए अनुमेय कटौतियों की गणना करे।
3. कुल वार्षिक कर देयता का निर्धारण करे।
4. पिछले नियोक्ता द्वारा पहले ही काटे गए टीडीएस का क्रेडिट देते हुए, शेष कर को बचे हुए महीनों (सितंबर से मार्च) के दौरान समान मासिक किस्तों में काटे।

यदि पिछले वेतन को छोड़ दिया जाए, तो कर्मचारी को दोहरी मूल छूट और मानक कटौती का अनुचित लाभ मिल जाएगा, जिससे कर की गंभीर अल्प-कटौती होगी।

questions.question_english: Under the Schedule to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, under which of the following broad classifications is 'Deafblindness' categorized?
options_english: Physical Disability
Multiple Disabilities
Intellectual Disability
Chronic Neurological Conditions
questions.explanation_english:
Under the Schedule of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 (specifying disabilities under Section 2(zc)), disabilities are broadly organized into specified categories including Physical Disability, Intellectual Disability, Mental Illness, Disabilities caused by Chronic Neurological Conditions & Blood Disorders, and Multiple Disabilities.

Section 2(zc) read with the Schedule defines 'Multiple Disabilities' as the occurrence of more than one of the specified disabilities in an individual, explicitly including 'Deafblindness'. Deafblindness is characterized as a distinct condition caused by a combination of both severe visual and hearing impairments, creating severe communication, developmental, educational, and mobility challenges. It cannot be accommodated simply as a single sensory impairment, which is why Parliament designated it under the Multiple Disabilities category to ensure specialized rehabilitation, tactile communication methods, and assistive pedagogical aids in educational institutions.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम (RPwD Act), 2016 की धारा 2(zc) के साथ पठित अनुसूची (Schedule) में विनिर्दिष्ट दिव्यांगताओं (Specified Disabilities) को विभिन्न श्रेणियों में वर्गीकृत किया गया है। इनमें शारीरिक दिव्यांगता, बौद्धिक दिव्यांगता, मानसिक रुग्णता, दीर्घकालिक तंत्रिका संबंधी एवं रक्त विकार तथा 'बहु-दिव्यांगता' शामिल हैं।

अनुसूची के पैरा 5 के अंतर्गत 'बहु-दिव्यांगता' (Multiple Disabilities) के तहत दो या दो से अधिक विनिर्दिष्ट दिव्यांगताओं के संयोजन को शामिल किया गया है, जिसमें स्पष्ट रूप से 'बधिर-अंधता' (Deafblindness) का उल्लेख किया गया है। बधिर-अंधता दृष्टि और श्रवण दोनों प्रकार की गंभीर क्षतियों का ऐसा मिला-जुला रूप है जिसके कारण गंभीर संचार, विकासात्मक और अधिगम संबंधी बाधाएं उत्पन्न होती हैं। इसलिए कानून में इसे एकल संवेदी बाधा न मानकर 'बहु-दिव्यांगता' के अंतर्गत रखा गया है ताकि ऐसे शिक्षार्थियों को विशेष स्पर्श संचार (स्पर्श ब्रेल), अनुरूपित शिक्षण और पुनर्वास सेवाएं प्रदान की जा सकें।

options_english: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala

questions.explanation_english: The introduction of Article 15(4) through the First Constitutional Amendment Act of 1951 was directly prompted by the Supreme Court's landmark judgment in State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (AIR 1951 SC 226). In this case, the Supreme Court invalidated the Madras Government's Communal Government Order (G.O.) that fixed admission quotas in state-run medical and engineering colleges based on religion, caste, and community. The Court held that admissions based on communal quotas infringed the fundamental right guaranteed under Article 29(2) and that Directive Principles (Article 46) could not override Fundamental Rights. Recognizing that affirmative action in education had no constitutional protection analogous to employment reservation under Article 16(4), Parliament amended Article 15 to insert clause (4), thereby explicitly shielding affirmative action admissions from Article 29(2) challenges.
questions.explanation_hindi: संविधान (प्रथम संशोधन) अधिनियम, 1951 के माध्यम से अनुच्छेद 15(4) का समावेश सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के ऐतिहासिक वाद 'मद्रास राज्य बनाम चंपकम दोराइराजन (AIR 1951 SC 226)' की सीधी विधायी प्रतिक्रिया थी। इस मामले में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने मद्रास सरकार के उस 'कम्युनल जी.ओ.' को निरस्त कर दिया था, जिसके तहत राज्य के मेडिकल और इंजीनियरिंग कॉलेजों में धर्म और जाति के आधार पर सीटें बांटी गई थीं। न्यायालय ने अभिनिर्धारित किया कि यह अनुच्छेद 29(2) (राज्य-पोषित संस्थानों में प्रवेश में भेदभाव के विरुद्ध अधिकार) का उल्लंघन करता है और राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व (अनुच्छेद 46) मौलिक अधिकारों का अतिक्रमण नहीं कर सकते। उस समय अनुच्छेद 16(4) की भांति शिक्षा के क्षेत्र में सकारात्मक कार्रवाई के लिए कोई विशिष्ट प्रावधान नहीं था। अतः संसद ने तुरंत प्रथम संशोधन के जरिए अनुच्छेद 15(4) जोड़ा ताकि SC, ST और पिछड़े वर्गों के लिए शैक्षणिक आरक्षण को संवैधानिक वैधता प्राप्त हो सके।

questions.question_english: Under Section 14 of the POSH Act, 2013, which of the following does NOT constitute a false or malicious complaint punishable under the law?
options_english: A complaint filed with the deliberate, clear malicious intent of defaming or harassing the respondent.
A complaint submitted along with forged, fabricated, or misleading documentary evidence.
A genuine complaint where the aggrieved woman is unable to substantiate the allegations with eyewitness corroboration.

questions.explanation_english:
Section 14 of the POSH Act, 2013 governs punishment for false or malicious complaints and false evidence.
Importantly, the Second Proviso to Section 14(1) explicitly provides:
'Provided further that the mere inability to substantiate a complaint or provide adequate proof need not attract action against the complainant under this section.'
Sexual harassment often occurs behind closed doors without direct eyewitnesses. The law consciously protects women from being penalized merely because they could not produce corroborating eyewitnesses or conclusively prove the charge. Action can only be taken if an inquiry establishes that the complaint was made with deliberate malicious intent or that forged/misleading documents were produced knowingly. Thus, an inability to substantiate does NOT constitute a false complaint.

Section 34(1) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 provides:
